title: fix(cli): os migrate meta --stored says what holds for each failed row, and names a flow the engine refuses at boot
body:
Fixes #23391
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`os migrate meta --stored` (human output) closes a run that reports `failed` rows with one line. It used to say every such row "keeps reading canonically through the chain, so nothing is broken". Measured on a real boot, that is false for two of the stored pass's four failed kinds. The `report.failed > 0` branch of `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts` now says:

- what holds for every failed kind: the pass wrote nothing, so each row stays as stored and reads as it did before the run, until the reason printed beside it is fixed;
- that this does not mean it works: a row whose stored body is not valid JSON does not load at all;
- only when a failed row is a flow (gated on the row's `type`, never on its reason's prose): a flow whose reason says it does not canonicalize is refused by the engine at boot as well, so it is not registered and does not run.

FROM: "N row(s) could not be rewritten. They keep reading canonically through the chain, so nothing is broken — but their stored bytes stay legacy until the reason above is fixed."

TO: "N row(s) could not be rewritten. Each stays as stored, and reads as it did before this run, until the reason printed beside it is fixed. That does not mean it works: a row whose stored body is not valid JSON does not load at all, and a flow whose reason says it does not canonicalize is refused by the engine at boot as well, so it is not registered and does not run."

The report, its row reasons, the exit code (1) and the `--json` payload are unchanged. `--json` carries no such sentence and is not touched. One `@objectstack/cli` patch changeset carries FROM and TO.

## The four failed kinds, measured

Producers read on `origin/main` `0d3ea295d1`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (read only):

| Producer | Kind | Reached on |
|---|---|---|
| `:23352` | the stored body is not valid JSON | any type, preview and apply |
| `:23405` | the flow does not canonicalize (`canonicalizeStoredFlow` threw) | flow, preview and apply |
| `:23417` | conversion refused over a live name (ADR-0078 conflict) | flow, preview and apply |
| `:23550` | the store refused the rewrite (`INVALID_METADATA`, `ITEM_LOCKED`, `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, a moved checksum, a 5xx) | any type, apply only |

A row stored organization-scoped is `skipped`, not `failed`.

Measured on a real composition: an ObjectKernel, ObjectQLPlugin's protocol over driver-sql on a better-sqlite3 file, and the real automation plugin. The rows were written into `sys_metadata` in a first boot, then a second boot was read (a throwaway harness in the shape of `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts`, not committed):

| Kind | What the second boot did with the row | The old claim |
|---|---|---|
| not valid JSON (a `flow` row, a `view` row) | the flow is not registered; `getMetaItem` of the row answers `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | false: it does not load |
| flow that does not canonicalize (a top-level key `FlowSchema` refuses) | `getFlow` is `null`; the item read carries `registration: refused` with the parse error | false: it does not run |
| flow conversion refused over a live name (`webhook` owned by a live executor) | registered, its node still `webhook`, the read says `registered` | "canonically" is false (the rename was skipped); whether it registers also depends on registration checks this kind never runs |
| the store refused the rewrite | nothing is written: `protocol.stored-migration.test.ts` pins the row untouched after an `INVALID_METADATA` refusal and after a moved checksum | "reads as before" holds by construction |

Why "not registered" holds for every flow of the second kind: `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` calls the same private `canonicalizeFlow` (convert, `FlowSchema.parse`, cycle check, region validator) that `canonicalizeStoredFlow` throws from. So every boot step that registers the body refuses it. The kernel:ready bind withdraws it and records the refusal (`flow-cold-boot-refusal-withdraw.test.ts`, `flow-refused-registration-read.integration.test.ts`). The sentence makes no claim about the read: in the mixed case below, that read answers `unregistered`, not `refused`.

## Pin, control, ablation

`packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-stored-failed.test.ts` (unit tier) runs the real command with the boot replaced and the real `formatStoredMigrationReport`:

1. A failed flow row: the line carries the shared sentence and the flow sentence, carries no "nothing is broken", and exits 1.
2. Control: a failed `view` row (not valid JSON) carries the shared sentence and the JSON sentence, with no flow sentence.
3. Mixed, on `--apply`: one line counting both rows, carrying both sentences.

Each ablation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with a restore trap. Both legs were committed first; each mutation's landing and restore were proven on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed; after the run, blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty). The pin imports `meta.ts` by relative source path, so no build was needed between legs.

- Leg 1 put back the retired sentence: 3 of 3 red. The flow pin failed with `Received: "  ✗ 1 row(s) could not be rewritten. They keep reading canonically through the chain, so nothing is broken — …"`.
- Leg 2 forced the flow gate false: the flow pin and the mixed pin went red, and the non-flow control stayed green (2 failed, 1 passed).

## Verification

All at `fb8ae99116` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `0d3ea295d1`). Builds and tests ran through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build`: exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`: "OK", nothing new in the debt ledger). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new test file (1 hit).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: 286 files passed. 2 files failed only on their build prerequisite: `published-subpath-console.pin` and `published-subpath-hook-body.pin` threw "packages/cli is not built", because the closure build excludes `cli` itself. After `cli` was built, those two plus the new pin passed: 3 files, 32 tests. The integration tier is left to CI: no integration file and no spawn entry is touched.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 65 commands. On the first pass, 63 exited 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: unbuilt dists); both exited 0 on a rerun once those dists existed. `--ran`: "65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED", exit 0.
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, whole repo): exit 0, no output.
- Control-byte scan of the three changed files: no match.

## Acceptance notes

- One finding, raised for the seat to file (class (a)). Measured at `protocol.getMetaItems` / `getMetaItemsForExecution`, the producers `GET /api/v1/meta/:type` and the cold-boot bind read. One stored row whose body is not valid JSON makes its whole type's list read answer `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` ("The metadata store could not be read…"), though the store was read. A row of another type is unaffected, and so is an item read of another row of the same type. For `flow`, that list is the kernel:ready bind's read, so the bind does nothing. A flow only the bind refuses then stays registered and enabled from the boot pull, and a parse-refused flow reads `unregistered`, not `refused`. The control without the invalid row: the same flow is withdrawn and reads `refused`. This PR does not change it; the CLI sentence claims only what holds either way ("does not load at all").
- The report carries no field naming a failed row's kind, so the CLI cannot tell the four apart without matching reason prose. That is why the flow sentence is keyed to the reason the operator reads and gated on `type`. A structured kind on `StoredMigrationRow` would let each line name its own consequence. Noted, not filed.
